title: Onboarding eval scripts and CI sketch
content:
Purpose

Working sketch for the eval harness artifacts we need to onboard a new model into Redwood’s production evaluation pipeline. This is intentionally rough — focuses on the minimal set of scripts, loaders, scoring functions and CI hooks we can ship in the next cycle. Use this as the canonical short-term checklist for onboards.

Goals
- fast repeatable evals for model candidates (local + CI)
- deterministic scoring and regression detection
- lightweight infra: run on GH Actions for quick checks, k8s batch for nightly/full/e2e
- clear developer DX: `make eval-quick` and `make eval-nightly`

Overview of components (high level)
1) loaders/formatters: small library to normalize datasets into a common record schema.
   - input formats supported: jsonl (preferred), csv, parquet, simple ndjson.
   - each loader returns flat records: { "id", "prompt", "context?", "expected_output", "meta" } — flatten nested fields.
   - canonical loader interface (python pseudocode):
     class DatasetLoader:
         def __init__(self, path: str, split: str = 'test'): ...
         def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[Dict[str, Any]]: ... # yields records above
         def metadata(self) -> Dict[str,str]: ...
   - implement adapters for: SQuAD-like QA, multiple-choice, free-gen, chat-turn pairs (role-based).
   - small util: `normalize_prompt(record)` handles templating, slot-filling, and prompt length checks.

2) prompt sets and prompt templating
   - store prompt templates separately from dataset content: `/prompts/{task}/{variant}.tpl`
   - runtime combines template + record to produce final prompt(s). Keep variants small (1-5) and name them explicitly e.g. `concise-qa-v1`, `step-by-step-v2`.
   - for chat models, formalize role tokenization (system/user/assistant) in the template format.

3) scoring functions
   - minimal built-ins: exact_match, normalized_edit_distance (levenshtein / token-level), token_overlap_ratio, logprob_thresholding (for hallucination detection), embedding_similarity (cosine on sentence embeddings).
   - API: score(pred: str, expected: str, record_meta: Dict) -> Dict[str, float|string] e.g. {"score":0.0, "match_type":"partial", "notes":"generated extra sentence"}
   - composite metrics: weighted aggregation (configurable per task). Example config for QA: {exact_match:0.6, emb_sim:0.4} with thresholds.
   - fuzzy-match rules: strip punctuation, normalize numbers/dates, map common aliases from a small token map. Keep this map editable per-dataset.

4) regression detection and reporting
   - baseline: compare new-run vs baseline run (artifact in S3 / GCS). Compute delta for each metric and flag if delta < -alpha where alpha is task-specific.
   - statistical tests: bootstrap CI for mean difference; flag regressions that are statistically significant at p < 0.05. Quick-mode: simple binomial test for exact-match-like metrics.
   - report artifact: csv + small html summary + per-record diagnostics .jsonl (include prompt, pred, expected, metric scores, diffs).
   - human-review queue: auto-generate `regression-sampler.csv` with stratified sampling of worst regressions + random baseline samples for annotation.

5) scripts and CLIs (what we need now)
   - tools/eval_run.py --config <yaml> --out <dir>  # runs an eval locally or against hosted model endpoint
   - tools/compare_runs.py --baseline <run> --candidate <run> --out report/  # produce regression report
   - tools/generate_promptset.py --dataset <path> --template <tpl> --out prompts/  # preview prompt combos
   - Makefile targets: `eval-quick` (100 examples), `eval-smoke` (10 example smoke), `eval-nightly` (full test split), `eval-ci` (integration smoke + regression check)

6) CI wiring (GitHub Actions sketch)
   - On PR to model onboarding / eval changes: run `eval-smoke` against a canned local model (docker image or small distil model) to catch runtime failures and major regressions. Exit nonzero on hard failures (exceptions) or critical regressions.
   - Nightly: full eval against dedicated infra (k8s job, larger GPU fleet). Post artifacts to `gs://redwood-evals/nightly/YYYY-MM-DD/{model}/{run}` and create a regression ticket if critical.
   - Example GH Action steps (conceptual):
     - checkout
     - setup python, install -e .[dev]
     - docker-compose up -d smokemodel  # optional local model container
     - make eval-smoke
     - upload run artifacts (actions/upload-artifact)
     - run compare_runs.py against most recent baseline (download from GCS)
     - comment results into PR with summary (use small html snippet previews)

Integration hooks to other infra
- storage: canonical artifact layout: `gs://redwood-evals/{env}/{model}/{run-id}/` with files: `run-metadata.json`, `predictions.jsonl`, `metrics.csv`, `regression-sample.csv`, `report.html`
- alerting: slack webhook on critical regression (channel: #eval-regressions) and create JIRA if severity high
- tracing: include `trace_id` in run-metadata for request-level debugging (maps to Redwood Console trace if run against hosted endpoint)

Edge cases and gotchas (notes)
- variable outputs: for open-ended tasks rely on embedding-similarity + human review; don't over-trust automatic pass/fail.
- tokenization mismatches: canonicalize on model tokenizer when possible (we have a small util to call tokenizers via container to avoid drift).
- long context truncation: loader should annotate tokenized_length and return `truncation=true|false` flag to allow filtering in quick runs.
- timeouts and partial outputs: scorer must detect partial stream outputs (e.g. <eos> missing) and penalize or mark for human review.

Local developer flow (recommended)
1. Add dataset to `datasets/raw/{dataset-name}/{split}.jsonl` with minimal schema.
2. Add prompt templates to `prompts/{dataset}/{variant}.tpl`.
3. Add `eval-configs/{dataset}-{variant}.yaml` referencing loader + scoring config + baseline run id (optional).
4. Run `make eval-quick` and inspect `out/latest/` outputs.
5. Create PR; CI runs eval-smoke and posts summary.

Open TODOs (short list)
- finalize canonical record schema and publish to Confluence (link below).
- pick default composite metric weights per task (work with product on loss tolerance).
- implement fast embedding cache for baseline runs to speed repeated comparisons.
- small web viewer for `report.html` with per-record diff highlighting (low priority but huge UX win).

References / links
- GH PR with current harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/214
- current orchestration playbook (Confluence): CONFLUENCE-ML/EVALS-bridge
- onboarding ticket exemplar: JIRA-EVAL-312

Notes to reviewers
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic: prefer small, well-specified tools to a big monolith. Where possible, prefer determinism (seeded RNGs, stable tokenizer versions) and clear outputs so product/CS can triage regressions quickly.
- If you have a dataset or task pattern that's not covered by the loader sketches above (e.g., multimodal image+text), add an item in the PR checklist and we’ll prioritize an adapter.

Quick snippets (copy-paste)
- run quick eval: `python tools/eval_run.py --config eval-configs/chatbot-concise-v1.yaml --out out/last --sample-size 100`
- compare: `python tools/compare_runs.py --baseline gs://redwood-evals/baselines/chatbot/2024-09-30 --candidate out/last --out out/compare`
- sample change for GH Actions: add `- name: Eval smoke
  run: make eval-smoke || (python tools/compare_runs.py --baseline gs://redwood-evals/baselines/ci-smoke --candidate out/last && exit 1)`

-- Priya

(Notes: leave comments inline in this doc for clarifications. Will move to Confluence after we stabilize schema.)
